$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 task `p2-g1-g2-analyze-band` (G1 Analyze, G2 Band, the lemma ledger). `owned` is EMPTY and the ids sit in `ownedPendingP2PhaseRoster`. That is not the same parking as the previous round: the refuter's stated cause (coverage-map.ts cannot see a Python test) IS FIXED on this branch and is proven non-vacuous. What is left is a second, larger gate the refuter did not see, it is P2-WIDE, and it is measured below rather than asserted.

coverageMapPythonSupport.what: scripts/coverage-map.ts scanned TEST_ROOTS = ['packages', 'apps', 'e2e'] with TEST_FILE_PATTERN = /\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$|\.ya?ml$/ and a JS-only claim regex, so the content pipeline's invariants could not be owned. INV-PACK-13/15/17 hit the same hole next.
landedHere: SKIP_DIRS gains .venv, .ruff_cache, .pytest_cache and __pycache__ — a coursekit venv carries thousands of installed test_*.py files

claimedIdsInPython(): a Python test claims the bracketed ids LEADING its docstring, mirroring it('[INV-DAY-01] …'). Leading only, because test_ledger_unit.py has a docstring reading '[INV-PACK-40] INV-MOD-13 stores speaking tokens …' — a whole-docstring scan would have reported INV-MOD-13 as covered, silently, in a green run
--self-test gains the Python reader, including that a module docstring, a non-test def, an assertion message and a prose citation all claim nothing
coverageMapPythonSupport.laneNote: scripts/coverage-map.ts is outside this task's declared file lane. It was changed here because the refuter's finding is that neither owned id is enforced without it, no other P2 lane touches the file (checked across all eight branches), and the change unblocks every other coursekit lane's ids too. Flagged for the integrate lane rather than done quietly.
coverageMapPythonSupport.status: LANDED on this branch and proven non-vacuous: with the ids in `owned`, `pnpm test:coverage-map` exits 0 and names both; rewriting the bracketed claims in the two Python test files to parentheses makes it exit 1 with 'no owning test for: INV-PACK-51'. Before this change nothing under tools/ was scanned at all.

blockers.severity: blocks every P2 lane, not just this one
blockers.what: packages/core/src/journey/phase-roster.test.ts compares the union of EVERY docs/owned/*.json against a roster derived from P1_FAMILIES in packages/core/src/journey/ownership.ts. That list is [SESS GRD COM MIS SCH DAY FRZ REC ECO CER PATH PER DAT] plus INV-SEC-01/02. PACK and AUD are not families in it; the eleven §13/§14 engine parts P1 does own are enumerated by hand in docs/owned/journey.json `engineParts`. So ANY P2 id in ANY ownership file is rejected as 'claimed but not in the P1 roster', and the count assertion ('the phase owns what the plan says it owns') hard-codes 217.
measured: With owned = [INV-PACK-40, INV-PACK-51]: `pnpm test` = 4 failed / 1254 passed, 2 files — phase-roster.test.ts (3) and falsifier-corpus.test.ts (1).

This is NOT specific to this lane. Putting p2/g7-expand's own claim INV-PACK-07 into an ownership file and running phase-roster.test.ts alone reproduces it verbatim: 3 failed, same message. p2/g3-g4 (INV-PACK-06), p2/g5-g6 (INV-PACK-10, INV-PACK-14), p2/g7 (INV-PACK-07/08/50), p2/g8 (INV-PACK-15, INV-AUD-08) and p2/g9 (INV-PACK-17, INV-PACK-41) have already written ids into `owned`, so five P2 branches carry this failure latently and it surfaces the moment any of them is merged.
threeSeparateHalves: 1. THE ROSTER. ownership.ts needs a P2 roster (the `C`-kind PACK/AUD ids) and phase-roster.test.ts needs to compare each ownership file against its own phase's roster instead of every file against P1's. The count 217 moves with it.

2. THE SCANNER. ownership.ts `owningTests()` has its own copy of the TS-only walk — TEST_ROOTS = ['packages','apps','e2e'], /\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$|\.ya?ml$/ — so even once the roster admits a PACK id, a Python-owned one still reads as 'no owning test' there. The fix is the one this branch already landed in scripts/coverage-map.ts (claimedIdsInPython + 'tools' + the venv skips); the two scanners should share one implementation rather than get the fix twice.

3. THE FALSIFIER CORPUS. falsifier-corpus.test.ts requires a committed falsifying input under packages/core/src/journey/falsifiers/ for every owned id. This lane's falsifiers are real and committed but live where the code that reads them lives: tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-40.json (5 cases) and INV-PACK-51.json (4 cases), each read by the tests by case id. That test needs to know a coursekit id's falsifier lives in the coursekit tree.
blockers.whoFixesIt: the P2 integrate task, or a P1-journey follow-up — packages/core/src/journey/ is outside every P2 lane's file ownership, and 'what the phase owns' is a phase accounting decision, not a lane's to make unilaterally
blockers.thenDo: move the two ids from `ownedPendingP2PhaseRoster` into `owned`
blockers.untilThen: the two ids are covered by 22 id-carrying tests (15 for INV-PACK-40, 7 for INV-PACK-51) that run in pack-ci.yml's pytest, and `pnpm test:coverage-map` reports them as OK the moment they are moved — verified by moving them, running it (exit 0, 'OK INV-PACK-40 <- 15 test(s)', 'OK INV-PACK-51 <- 7 test(s)'), and moving them back.

resolvedSinceTheFirstReview.what: This lane registers g1 and g2, so test_cli.py::test_discovery_finds_nothing_yet_and_that_is_the_correct_state no longer described reality — and it passed anyway, over a registry that Registry.reset_for_tests() had left permanently empty (reset cleared `_discovered`, but discover() re-imports through importlib, which is a sys.modules cache hit, so no @register_stage ever fired again).
resolvedSinceTheFirstReview.resolution: ALREADY FIXED ON `p2/validate-sample-ci`, which owns tests/test_cli.py, tests/conftest.py and src/coursekit/__init__.py. That branch rewrites the assertion as a relationship (missing() is the complement of ids()), adds restore_for_tests() that evicts the imported modules from sys.modules, and adds test_resetting_the_registry_lets_discovery_run_again. Duplicating it here would have guaranteed a merge conflict on three files this lane does not own. Verified by test-merging the two branches — see the report's evidence.

resolvedSinceTheFirstReview.what: `p2-deps-scaffold` created empty config/analyze.py (owner 'p2-g1-analyze') and config/band.py (owner 'p2-g2-band') beside this lane's live config/g1.py and config/g2.py.
resolvedSinceTheFirstReview.resolution: DELETED in this branch. Nothing imported them (checked). Two plausible homes for a ledger constant is how the second declaration gets written, and INV-PACK-40's 'declared exactly once' test greps for the name LEDGER_UNIT_BY_LANGUAGE — it would not have caught a window or a budget landing in the twin. The naming notes at the top of config/g1.py and config/g2.py were updated to say they are gone.

foundersEyesOnly: THE DECILE PROXY IS NOT CALIBRATED, AND THE NUMBER IS NOW MEASURED. scope2/00 line 110 specifies the G2 fallback as a 'frequency-decile proxy calibrated against fr/es/de/en'. config/g2.BAND_BY_DECILE is hand-picked. scripts/calibrate_band_deciles.py measures it on the real inputs (hermitdave es_50k.txt, the published ELELex.tsv, es_core_news_md 3.8.0): 33,685 ledger lemmas, 7,508 covered by ELELex, and the shipped table agrees with the lexicon on 38.0% of them. The best monotone fit reaches 41.2%. The shipped table was KEPT and the deviation recorded, for three reasons written into the constant's docstring: the fit buys 3.2 points and costs three of the five bands (it can never emit B2 or C1, and calls everything below the top decile A2); `band` feeds G3's ordering and G7's distractor rule and the es-mini fixture four other P2 lanes test against was derived under the shipped table, so re-banding is a cross-lane change for a founder checkpoint; and the real finding is that a frequency decile explains about two fifths of a CEFR band either way — which is exactly why Q8 ships de/ja as 'Beginner · frequency-ordered · no CEFR resource' and never 'A1 · CEFR-checked'.

AND IT IS CALIBRATED AGAINST SPANISH ALONE WHILE GERMAN AND JAPANESE SHIP ON IT. The spec asks for fr/es/de/en. `de` is impossible — DAFlex publishes no files at all (no filenames, no counts, no tagger, 'reference article forthcoming', re-verified 2026-09-11). `en` is not a target language. `fr` is possible in principle (FLELex is published) but a calibration run needs a French adapter to lemmatise the French frequency list and this lane builds none. P7 should re-run the script with the French adapter and record whether the fit moves.
heldWithoutAnInvariantId: The adapter self-test corpus (config/g1.ADAPTER_SELFTEST_ES): twelve ORIGINAL A1 Spanish sentences and the exact surface/lemma/UPOS string es_core_news_md 3.8.0 produces for each, plus a sha256 the adapter checks at import so the table and its digest cannot drift apart. It exists because the wheel-URL pin is not sufficient on its own: a contributor's stale venv, a patched spaCy or a stray spacy-lookups-data re-partitions the lemma ledger, which retro-introduces lemmas before their introduction unit and makes V1 pass vacuously — every test downstream of G2 re-derives the ledger with the new lemmatiser and agrees with itself. The sentences sit on the seams (al/del contractions, clitic se, gender and number agreement, ser/estar, existential hay, preterite) and four of the frozen answers are wrong Spanish (Nosotros->yo, se->él, muy->mucho, trabajé unlemmatised) and are frozen anyway, because the table records what the pinned model DOES

hermitdave's CC BY-SA 4.0 duty is discharged in code, not in a comment: g2_band writes derived_ordering_licence, derived_ordering_share_alike and a named attribution string into the runlog, and a test asserts all three on a real run. An ordering derived from CC BY-SA content is a derivative of it; the pack's CC BY-NC-SA is compatible, but shipping it without declaring it redistributes an SA derivative without passing the licence on

config/g2.ELELEX_LICENCE carries the reasoning beside the constant, and a test greps for it: ELELex is CC BY-NC-SA and is usable HERE ONLY because the plan's licence split makes packs CC BY-NC-SA while code stays AGPL-3.0. The block states what may not be done with it — never vendored into this repository, never moved into packages/ or apps/ — because the next person to find the constant will be looking for something to reuse

ELELEX_POS_MUST_MATCH now means what its name says, and both branches are pinned by a test. It used to read `lexicon.get((lemma, pos)) if ELELEX_POS_MUST_MATCH else None` over a lexicon already keyed by POS, so setting it False disabled ELELex banding entirely: every es/fr pack fell back to the decile proxy while band_source truthfully read `frequency_decile` and the course card still read 'CEFR-checked'. True now refuses the band and counts `cefr_pos_disagreements`; False takes the lemma-matched band under the distinct source name `cefrlex_pos_relaxed` and counts `cefr_pos_relaxed`. Both counts reach the runlog, because a POS disagreement is otherwise indistinguishable from a lemma the lexicon never carried

R23 is enforced structurally, not just documented: banded_lemma has no section_cefr field, unit_assignment does, and a test asserts both plus that build_rows never emits one. The measured product attaches CEFR to SECTIONS (Spanish ships 8: 1-3 A1, 4 A2, 5-6 B1, 7-8 B2), which is a G3 curriculum output; a per-lemma lexicon cannot produce it and a frequency decile cannot either

NEW FINDING, same class as R3 and R11: `deep/10` §S4 says ELELex's FreeLing POS maps via `freeling_to_elelex.yaml` beside the TSV. That path 404s (verified 2026-09-12, four spellings; the server answers with 1,165 bytes of HTML, so an unchecked fetch gets an error page and a mapping of nothing). config/g2.FREELING_TO_UD is ours, written against the EAGLES tagset and the 40 distinct tags the published file actually contains, and multiword rows ('NCM, NP0', 'VM VM') map to nothing rather than being guessed at

NEW FINDING, measured: a bare surface form is a bad place to read a POS from. es_core_news_md tags 6.1% of the top 3,000 Spanish surface forms as PROPN when each is its own one-token document — casa, perro and hola among them — which would split casa/PROPN from casas/NOUN into two ledger rows, the exact failure lemmatising hermitdave's list exists to prevent. So G2 takes the POS from G1's in-context corpus wherever the corpus has the lemma, falls back to the context-free tag only for the tail, consolidates a lemma's competing tags onto the one with the most evidence, and reports all four counts

ELELex's banding threshold is calibrated against the real file rather than chosen: at >= 1 document per level the 14,290 entries partition completely (A1 3674 / A2 3576 / B1 3018 / B2 2119 / C1 1903); at >= 3 documents 9,430 of them fall out and silently revert to the decile proxy while the pack still claims CEFR-checked. The distribution is in the constant's docstring so raising the number is a visible decision

The ledger key is case-folded on BOTH elements. reading_form() used to NFC-normalise without folding while normalized_form() folded, so ledger_key('es','Casa','NOUN') and ledger_key('es','casa','NOUN') were two keys — two rows in one learner's Words list — and the 'one item' guarantee rested on the spaCy adapter calling .lower() on every lemma rather than on the ledger, which is the second definition INV-PACK-40 exists to forbid. Folding katakana is a no-op, so the Japanese branch is unchanged

The frequency list is read from a LOCAL file and G2 never fetches: a stage that downloads on demand makes every run depend on whatever `master` says today, which is the same moving-input hazard the spaCy wheel-URL pin exists for. A short file, and a 404 HTML body, are both refused by name rather than read as a language with no vocabulary. The filename is also tied to the source URL by a test, because it was knowledge in two places

G1 reports mean content-words-per-sentence for the pack and fails the stage when any sentence falls outside the pack's own length window. That second check is the numeric half of INV-PACK-40's grep gate: a G0 that counted its own tokens lets through sentences the ledger measures outside the window, and the code gate cannot see a pre-built G0 output. The mean itself now goes through the same split_mode-vs-declaration guard as the counter — a ja Mode-C row used to be refused by count_units and silently averaged by the one figure that reaches the manifest
